title: Great Is the Lord Our God
description: Great Is the Lord Our God in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 48, part 1, headed “The church is the honour and safety of a nation”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Great is the Lord our God, And let his praise be great; He makes his church-es his a-bode, His most de-light-ful seat.

lines: Great is the Lord our God,
And let his praise be great;
He makes his churches his abode,
The honours of our native place,
How bright has his salvation shone
And saw the Lord was there,
In wild confusion of the mind
He sends his tempests roaring loud,
And sinks them in the seas.
How well our God secures the fold
Where his own sheep have been.
We'll think upon his wondrous grace,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
